opening.welcome: You are painting a misty autumn birch grove, with a leaf-covered path running back into the fog. The two big leaning birches are the heart of it, pale bark against a glowing gold haze. Keep the far things soft and the near things bold, and the mist will do the rest.
opening.light: A low sun shines through the wood from behind the trees, so the gold bushes and leaves nearest it glow while the pines sit in cool blue shade. The birches and the rock catch that sun on the side facing it and fall into shadow away from it.

skills.how: Dabbing is tapping with the tip of a dry brush, so the paint lands as separate dots that turn into leaves. It builds the bushes, the leaves overhead and the fallen leaves, always dark first, then middle, then the sunlit ones. Keep the brush dry and lightly loaded, or the dots turn into blobs.

Dry brush is a nearly dry brush skimmed lightly so the paint catches only the canvas texture. It makes the mist, the shadows on the path, and the soft shade and light on the birch bark. If it goes on solid, the brush was too loaded.

Thick to thin is pressing the brush's full width, then easing onto its edge so the mark tapers. It pulls the far trunks and the birches, wide at the foot and narrow as they rise, and makes the short dark bark marks.

opening.road: First comes the misty background, the farthest thing, so the depth is there before anything solid. Then the near woods: the pines and the golden bushes. Next the ground with its path and the mossy rock. The birches, the subject, go on over all of it, and then the gold leaves overhead and the fallen leaves go over the trunks. The brightest sunlit leaves come last. The first layers stop where the ground will cover them, so bare canvas showing early on is expected.

the-background.for: This stage lays the soft, misty fog that everything else stands in.
the-background.end: A soft blue fog with a faint warm glow and a few far trunks fills the back of the scene; the rest of the canvas is still bare.

the-near-woods.for: This stage adds the dark pines and the glowing golden bushes in front of the fog.
the-near-woods.end: Dark pines lit with soft green and a bright gold bush now stand in front of the fog; the rest of the canvas is still bare.

the-ground.for: This stage covers the ground with warm leaf color, runs the path back into the fog, and sets the mossy rock on it.
the-ground.end: The whole canvas is covered: an orange leafy ground with a pale path into the fog and a round, shaded rock at the foot of the pines.

the-birches.for: This stage stands the six birches over everything and gives them their patchy, dark-marked bark.
the-birches.end: Six birches stand in front of the woods, pale with gray patches and near-black marks heavy at their feet.

the-canopy.for: This stage hangs the golden leaves overhead, over the trunks.
the-canopy.end: Gold leaves hang in loose clusters over the trunks, with darker leaves peeking through and fog between.

the-fallen-leaves.for: This stage turns the ground into a carpet of separate fallen leaves.
the-fallen-leaves.end: The ground is a carpet of orange leaves with dark red-brown and gray ones between.

the-last-lights.for: This stage taps the brightest sunlit leaves where the sun falls, to finish the painting.
the-last-lights.end: The painting is finished: pale sunlit leaves glow overhead, on the big bush and along the path.
